Simulate dense or irregular Gaussian and Student-t functional trajectories with auditable truth

etr_simulate_functional_process.Rd

Native R simulation of bounded dense and irregular functional domains of frozen eyetrajectoriespy 1.2.0 simulate_functional_process. Declares curve, participant and trial random scores independently, retains latent trajectories and measurement-noise realizations, and supports either independent channel noise SDs or a symmetric positive-semidefinite cross-channel covariance matrix. No Python is required for native simulation.

Usage

etr_simulate_functional_process(
  mean, eigenfunctions, eigenvalues, truth_grid, n_participants,
  trials_per_participant = 1L, dimension_names = "value",
  coordinate_system = "unknown", time_unit = "normalized",
  observation_design = "dense", observation_times = NULL,
  samples_per_curve = NULL, irregular_time_design = "uniform",
  participant_eigenvalues = NULL, trial_eigenvalues = NULL,
  measurement_noise_sd = 0, measurement_noise_covariance = NULL,
  missingness = NULL, phase_variation = NULL,
  score_distribution = "normal", score_df = 5,
  orthonormal_tolerance = 1e-6, random_state = 42L,
  source_draws = NULL, random_engine = "base_R",
  python_boundary_mode = FALSE
)

Arguments

mean

Callable returning a source-compatible function of time.

eigenfunctions

List of source component evaluation callables.

eigenvalues

Positive, nonincreasing component variances.

truth_grid

Finite, strictly increasing common grid of at least three times.

n_participants

Number of independent participants.

trials_per_participant

Number of trials per participant.

dimension_names

Unique functional channel names.

coordinate_system,time_unit

Explicit trajectory coordinate and time units.

observation_design

"dense" uses the exact common truth grid; "irregular" returns native curve-specific schedules with no interpolation.

observation_times

For irregular simulation, an optional list containing exactly one finite, strictly increasing numeric time vector per curve, each with at least two samples within the truth-grid domain.

samples_per_curve

For irregular simulation only: a positive integer count (at least two) or a two-integer minimum/maximum range. Provide this or observation_times, not both. Both are NULL for dense.

irregular_time_design

Native generated irregular schedules use "uniform" (interior uniform 0.01 to 0.99), "center_clustered" (0.01 + 0.98 times Beta(4,4)), or "boundary_poor" (interior uniform 0.15 to 0.85). Endpoints are retained; generated times are sorted.

participant_eigenvalues,trial_eigenvalues

Optional nonnegative participant-level and trial-level component variances.

measurement_noise_sd

Nonnegative scalar or one independent measurement-noise standard deviation per channel. Must be zero when measurement_noise_covariance is supplied.

measurement_noise_covariance

Optional finite symmetric positive-semidefinite channel-by-channel covariance. If supplied, the simulator draws correlated Gaussian noise using an eigenvalue-based symmetric square root. The declared matrix is preserved in source truth and provenance. Cannot be combined with positive noise SD.

missingness

Optional named mapping list(kind="mcar",probability=p) or list(kind="block",fraction=f) with finite p/f in [0,1). MCAR masks each observation time independently; block masks one contiguous interval of size floor(fraction times n_samples), with at least one masked sample when fraction is positive. All channels share each curve's mask. Dense outputs retain NA; irregular outputs remove masked samples from the published schedule, retaining complete pre-missing truth.

phase_variation

NULL or a source power-phase mapping list(kind="power",sd=s) with finite nonnegative log-exponent standard deviation. Independently for each curve, the exponent is exp(Normal(0,s)); the latent mean and generating modes are evaluated directly at the transformed time, not interpolated or relabeled as new observation timestamps.

score_distribution

"normal" or "student_t". This controls curve-level functional component scores only. Participant-level and trial-level score effects remain Gaussian.

score_df

Degrees of freedom for "student_t", finite and greater than two. The source variance correction (score_df-2)/score_df makes each Student-t curve-score component's population variance equal to its declared eigenvalue. The parameter is not evaluated when score_distribution="normal".

orthonormal_tolerance

Positive finite numerical tolerance for source quadrature orthonormality.

random_state

Nonnegative integer seed for the selected engine. The NumPy engine accepts exactly represented seeds below \(2^{53}\).

random_engine

"base_R" preserves the legacy native stream. "numpy" uses native PCG64 to replay frozen Python 1.2 seed order for Gaussian and Student-t scores, generated schedules, phase, noise and dropout. The same option is available to etr_simulate_functional_scenario() and etr_run_functional_recovery_scenarios().

source_draws

Optional captured source curve, participant, trial and measurement-noise draws for exact paired Python/R value replay. When supplied, all four source fields must match declared geometry. Dense measurement_noise is a numeric curve-by-time-by-channel array; irregular measurement_noise is a list of one time-by-channel matrix per pre-missing curve. With declared missingness, an optional missingness_mask field contains one logical vector per curve; with declared power-phase variation, an optional phase_exponents field contains one finite positive numeric exponent per curve, allowing exact frozen-Python realized-mask and realized-warp replay with random_engine="base_R".

python_boundary_mode

If TRUE, follow declared published-source boundary semantics; FALSE retains native validation defaults.

Value

An etr_functional_simulation_result with observations as a native common-grid etr_trajectory_set or curve-specific etr_irregular_trajectory_set, and truth containing latent values, separated scores, Gaussian noise, named covariance, metadata, and provenance.

Details

The base-R engine uses its existing symmetric covariance square root. The NumPy engine consumes hierarchy scores before schedules and phase, then interleaves measurement noise and dropout for each curve. It skips noise draws when the entire covariance lies within \(10^{-8}\) of zero. NumPy-seeded covariance noise uses an SVD factor. Exact replay of its realization depends on the signed singular-vector basis returned by the local LAPACK backend, especially for tied singular values. Retained source draws remain available for cross-backend replay. The returned observation values use the native missing-data sentinel NA at masked samples, while truth$observed_pre_missing retains the complete noisy signal and truth$missingness_mask retains one logical vector per curve. No silent zero-imputation occurs. Irregular observation times are evaluated by the generating mean and eigenfunction callables directly, without interpolating the truth grid. Irregular missing samples are removed from the output curve/time lists; the full pre-missing arrays and logical masks remain in truth. Power-phase warps are available on both dense and irregular trajectories. Raw observation times remain unwarped; the complete-grid `truth$phase_warps_on_truth_grid` and the original/warped pre- and post-missing schedules are retained separately. The `truth$latent_on_truth_grid` and observed latent signals are evaluated at the warped time by the generating functions. Curve-level Student-t scores with finite degrees of freedom greater than two are implemented and preserve the source component variance. Participant and trial effects remain Gaussian. The qualified seeded cases cover finite explicit seeds, the documented simulation mechanisms and the resulting native truth fields. Python dataclass identity, broader coercion and exception domains, and independent scientific certification remain open.
